markdown_report:
### Insights and framework

Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. First, SASRec’s causal attention can mix recent and older interests; explicit recent evidence may reduce current-intent dilution. Second, isolated interactions do not establish equipment ownership or replacement needs; related-item recommendations require cautious support. Third, Electronics has 14.95% wrong sampled rankings and a −0.4812 lower-tail margin, motivating objective experiments without implying validation gains.

Three literature insights complement these observations. [GaGNN](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2024.120623) motivates training-derived transition evidence, although population transitions cannot prove individual compatibility. [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) motivates separating recent and sustained preferences, with uncertain transfer to sparse purchases. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates testing negative count and calibration; larger margins alone do not establish better ranking.

The conceptual map has three directions: **temporal evidence** (recent versus sustained interests), **relational evidence** (observed transitions versus broad associations), and **optimization** (negative coverage versus false-negative exposure). The proposed algorithm connects relational evidence to recent intent while testing optimization separately.

### Candidate assessment

Each cell gives a score/10, one strength (+), and one limitation (−). Difficulty increases with implementation effort.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recent/history pooling gate [LSIDN] | 3; +compact adaptation; −established | 6; +reusable; −sparse evidence | 7; +current intent; −no compatibility signal | 5; +context separation; −indirect margin effect | 3; +small branch; −writer changes |
| **Recent transition residual** [GaGNN] | 4; +evidence-conditioned scoring; −standard ingredients | 7; +interpretable support; −rare transitions | 8; +specific next steps; −ownership unproven | 6; +candidate discrimination; −no guaranteed gain | 4; +sparse counts; −prefix discipline |
| Sixteen-negative sampled softmax [gSASRec] | 2; +clean control; −established | 7; +strong baseline; −protocol dependence | 4; +ranking focus; −intent implicit | 8; +targets confusion; −false negatives | 3; +simple loss; −extra scoring |

### Selected idea: recent transition residual

At 0% progress, prioritize a small, reversible extension. Add a bounded transition score to SASRec using the last few interactions. Shrink rare transitions and discount globally popular destinations. This explicitly targets **broad relevance outranking current intent** and **unsupported upgrades**, by favoring empirically observed next steps over loose associations. These are hypotheses: transitions cannot establish compatibility or satisfied needs.

Build directed counts exclusively from training histories. Gate the residual using history length, transition support, and agreement across recent anchors. Initialize its contribution near zero.

```text
counts ← adjacent training transitions
for each causal training prefix:
    support ← shrunk, popularity-adjusted transitions from recent anchors
    score ← SASRec(prefix) + bounded_gate(prefix, support) × support
    optimize baseline loss
```

Keep sparse top-neighbor tables and identical inference scoring. Compare baseline, residual, and residual plus 16-negative softmax using pinned macro validation HR@10. Track Electronics’ margin tail separately; preserve all four routes, seeds, and diagnostic interfaces. No improvement is claimed before evaluation.

idea.description: Add an evidence-gated, recent directed-transition residual to the existing per-dataset SASRec scorer. Use sparse counts from adjacent training interactions, shrink low-support edges, and discount popular destinations. Bound the residual contribution and initialize it near zero.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations outranking recent intent and upgrades with insufficient supporting evidence. Recent observed transitions provide a testable signal for specific next steps, although they cannot verify equipment ownership or compatibility. Electronics’ weak sampled separation provides a model-facing reason to test whether this signal better distinguishes plausible candidates.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain the existing preprocessing, four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and SASREC_EPOCHS environment handling with the host default of 200. Construct counts from training histories only; never consult validation targets when constructing features. Use a small top-neighbor sparse table per source item. For edge (i,j), use a shrunk conditional probability multiplied by a clipped inverse-popularity factor; average across recent anchors with normalized recency weights. Normalize the resulting support to a bounded range. A small sigmoid gate can consume prefix length, total edge support, and agreement among anchors. Initialize the gate bias negatively. Begin with the baseline loss to isolate the scoring change; separately test 16 uniform negatives with sampled softmax, filtering padding, target collisions, and known training-history positives. Unobserved items remain uncertain negatives. The predictor writer must serialize transition tables, gate parameters, and identical score normalization beneath the trial directory. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Ensure view.model includes the gate and that predict_score uses the same combined scorer as inference. Features may carry recent-anchor information alongside sequence representations. Existing embedding diagnostics should explicitly measure the SASRec item embedding component. Avoid unavailable category-based breakdowns; report these as unavailable rather than fabricating values. Select only through the pinned macro validation HR@10; margins are supporting diagnostics.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset independently:
    C[i,j] = count of adjacent i -> j transitions in training histories
    out[i] = sum_j C[i,j]
    pop[j] = training interaction frequency of j
    A[i,j] = C[i,j] / (out[i] + shrinkage)
    A[i,j] *= clip((median_positive_pop / pop[j])**beta, lower, upper)
    retain top K edges per source

For every causal prefix x and candidate j:
    anchors = last W nonpadding items in x
    support[j] = weighted_mean(A[anchor,j], recency_weights)
    support[j] = bounded_normalize(support[j])
    evidence = [log1p(prefix_length), observed_edge_support, anchor_agreement]
    gate = sigmoid(MLP(evidence))  # small initial contribution
    score[j] = sasrec_score(x,j) + residual_scale * gate * support[j]

Train baseline-loss and residual-loss controls with identical seeds.
Optionally ablate 16-negative sampled softmax as a separate change.
Write an inference module that reproduces this exact score.
Select using the required four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Combines recent transition support, evidence-dependent shrinkage, and a bounded residual in a compact adaptation tailored to the observed failures.
originality.negative: Transition models, recency weighting, and gated fusion are established techniques; the contribution is an empirical combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides an interpretable basis for studying when specific behavioral evidence improves sequential recommendations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions may limit coverage, and observed purchase sequences do not certify functional compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sparse count construction and a small scoring extension without external encoders or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Training, diagnostic scoring, and generated inference must preserve identical prefix features and residual normalization.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal self-attention for sequential recommendation and supplies the starting architecture.
limitations: Does not explicitly require evidence of compatibility or distinguish satisfied needs from useful next purchases.

related_work.title: GaGNN
contributions: Combines group and individual transition graphs with collaborative and sequential encoders, motivating training-derived relational signals.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish improvements under the pinned RecHarness protocol.
Population transition evidence cannot establish individual equipment ownership.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Separates long-term and short-term interest modeling and uses augmentation for short-term robustness.
limitations: Transfer to sparse purchase histories and the exact four-category evaluation requires testing.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies overconfidence in negative-sampled BCE and introduces generalized BCE.
Motivates controlled comparisons of loss calibration and negative count.
limitations: Does not establish that the reported Electronics margin weakness is caused by BCE.
Improved sampled training margins need not improve validation HR@10.
